title: SK Chairman Choi Tae-won to Sell 2.3% SK Inc. Stake Worth ₩944B
content:
Korea Supply Chain Brief · October 2, 2026

SK Group Chairman Choi Tae-won will sell a 2.3% stake in holding company SK Inc., worth about 944 billion won, in an off-exchange deal starting November 2. Here's what's been disclosed about the sale structure and why it's happening.

CompanyRoleEvidence
SK Inc.
KRX: 034730		Holding company whose shares Chairman Choi Tae-won is sellingReported: company disclosure, Oct 2, 2026

What's been disclosed

  • Size of sale: Chairman Choi will divest 1,653,924 common shares of SK Inc., a 2.3% stake, valued at roughly 944 billion won.
  • Timing and method: The sale begins November 2, 2026, structured as an off-exchange transaction specifically to minimize impact on SK Inc.'s share price.
  • Deal structure: 544 billion won of the shares will go to strategic investors (SI), while the remaining 400 billion won will be sold via a principal-protected swap (PRS) with securities firms — a structure that lets Choi retain exposure to any future increase in the shares' value.
  • Resulting ownership: Choi's direct holding falls from 12,975,472 shares (17.8%) to 11,321,548 shares (15.5%). Including his own voting stake and related parties, his effective stake moves from roughly 20.8% individually to about 30.5% combined with related parties — he remains SK Inc.'s largest shareholder throughout.
  • Stated reason: The company attributed the sale to Choi's need for personal funds following an appellate court ruling in his divorce proceedings requiring a property-division payment.
  • Company statement: SK said the structure "minimizes market influence while maintaining management stability and the mid-to-long-term growth strategy."

Why this matters

A sale of this size by a group's controlling shareholder is often a share-price overhang risk, but the off-exchange structure and the SI/PRS split are specifically designed to avoid a direct supply shock to SK Inc.'s stock on the open market. Because Choi keeps economic exposure to the shares sold via PRS and remains the largest shareholder by a wide margin even after the sale, the disclosure frames this as a personal liquidity event tied to the divorce settlement rather than a change in control or strategy. (Reported)

What's still unconfirmed

The identities of the strategic investors (SI) taking the 544 billion won tranche, the specific securities firms involved in the 400 billion won PRS, and the exact terms of the PRS (duration, settlement price) were not disclosed. (Reported)

Quick FAQ

Does this change who controls SK Group?
No indication of that. Choi remains SK Inc.'s largest shareholder both individually and combined with related parties after the sale.

What is a PRS (principal-protected swap) in this context?
It lets Choi sell shares now for cash while keeping financial exposure to the stock's future price performance, rather than fully exiting that portion of his position.

Why is the stake being sold off-exchange instead of on the market?
The company said this structure was chosen specifically to minimize the sale's impact on SK Inc.'s share price, compared to selling that volume of shares on the open market.
